hyps.why: Edge 4 is a dead branch when node 1 has no input, so removing it is nearly free.
Node 2 is then mostly an identity copy of the input, redundant with edge 3, so cutting edge 5 loses little.
A strong conv alternative path to the output makes the direct edge less necessary.
A 1x1 conv adds little beyond what the skip already passes through, making it redundant.
The 1x1 conv is largely redundant next to an identity path into the output node.
Two consecutive pools on the 0->1->3 chain over-smooth the signal.
A skip from a conv-rich node 1 passes rich features to the output cheaply.
Edge 2 would add a conv-processed path from an identity-fed node 1, a meaningful route to the output.
A conv on edge 1 gives node 2 real features that pooling can smooth rather than blur raw input.
Removing edge 5 costs less when the node 2 contribution is already thinned.
